Hub/Website/Templates
Website

Templates.

Reusable structures, read from the designer's Figma pages and checked against the rules: the category page, the product page, where product and category colours go on a page, a page spec to fill before designing a new page, and the image slot convention. The colour swatches and their contrast table are on Foundations · Colour.

Category pageProduct pageProduct coloursCategory coloursPage specImage slots

Page templates.

Every new category reuses the category template; every product reuses the product template. No new section types per category. Each category carries its own colour on its hero band and dark sections (Category colours, below; R-117).

Category page · Sexual health (Figma 2708-1034)

  1. Header · launch menushort nav 2738-2783
  2. HeroHero 46/54 (34/40 mobile). "Better Intimacy" as editorial title; nav keeps "Sexual health". No Rx name, price or claim (R-58, R-65). Under the buttons: "[charge line · operations]" (R-62) and "Assessment only. Not a diagnosis." (R-63). Band in the category colour (R-117).
  3. Trust barFacts only, no ratings (R-67).
  4. IntroductionPlain description of the category.
  5. Product optionsOne card per product; names allowed here as they link to product pages with safety information. Each card marks its product with a dot and an edge in the product colour (R-85). Card title 24 (21 mobile), action "Learn more". Under the cards: "Prescription treatment is subject to provider approval. Results vary."
  6. How it worksThe one four-step wording (q132, Home section library), in the category colour (Deep Teal for Sexual health).
  7. EducationEditorial serif moment.
  8. FAQAccordion, 220ms.
  9. Final CTA"Get started" with "Assessment only. Not a diagnosis." (R-63).
  10. Medical noticeLicensed provider named (R-64).
  11. CTA band and footer2738-1094 · 2738-1012

Product page · Tadalafil (Figma 2076-11945)

  1. Header · launch menushort nav
  2. Product head (not a hero)The product name is the page title: DM Serif 46/54 at most, 34/40 on mobile, never the 70/60 hero size (R-20). Because this head is not a hero, the name is allowed; no benefit claim next to it (R-65). Strength and form under it ("Tadalafil, 20 mg tablets", R-108). The band stays the category colour; the product colour marks the name with a dot and a short bar (R-85).
  3. How it helpsPlain description; legal to review.
  4. BenefitsLegal review benefit language must be approved (R-58, R-65).
  5. What to expectProcess, not outcomes.
  6. CareThe licensed provider and ongoing support.
  7. Get startedCTA with "Assessment only. Not a diagnosis." and "[charge line · operations]" (R-62, R-63).
  8. FAQAccordion.
  9. ClosingEditorial line.
  10. SafetyImportant safety information, always fully expanded, linked from the hero (R-66).
  11. CTA band and footer2738-2581 · 2738-1104

Product colours.

Where a product colour appears on the website and the product page: as a dot or an edge beside the product name, never as a ground for text. Tokens --color-product-*; the hero band stays the category colour.

Current · R-85, U-28

Product colours mark their product wherever it is relevant on the website (O-03 closed): the product card (a dot or an edge), the product page accent, the product chip in menus and the recommendation card. They mark, they never carry text or data (text stays in the text colours) and never replace the category colour of the page (R-117). The product name always sits beside the colour, so colour is never the only key.

A dot or an edge, beside the name.

Dot 12, card edge 4 on the left, recommendation edge 4 on top, product page bar 48 × 4. Same sizes on mobile.

No text on a product colour.

A product colour is never a card ground, a button or a label behind words; Paper on Tadalafil Sky is 1.72:1.

Never instead of the category colour.

The hero band, the dark sections and the category tag keep the category colour (R-117). One product colour per card.

Category colours.

Each category page carries its family colour, the same colour as its label ground on the bottle. Shown on the two places it is strongest: the head (hero band) and the dark anchor section, for all three categories, on desktop and on mobile. The swatches, tokens and contrast ratios are on Foundations · Colour.

Current · R-117

Sexual health is Deep Teal (--color-category-sexual-health), Longevity is Forest (--color-category-longevity), Hair loss is Sky (--color-category-hair-loss). The category's hero band, its dark anchor sections and its category accents (eyebrow mark, tags, the category card on the home gateway, the menu marker) use the category colour. Yellow stays the single result moment. Contrast is AA: Paper text on Deep Teal and Forest, Deep Teal text on Sky. Sky is a light ground: its text, icons and buttons are Deep Teal.

Desktop · 1440.

Header, hero band, trust strip, a Paper section with the category tag, and the anchor section ("How it works"). Copy from the Figma category pages; photos are stand-ins, not approved.

Mobile · 390.

Same colours and the same order. The photo sits above the text, the two buttons stack at full width (44 px tall), the trust strip becomes two by two, the four steps become one column. The header carries the Primary seal, taller than the header button (R-103).

Contrast for text, icons and buttons on each category ground: Foundations · Colour. In short: Paper text on Deep Teal and Forest, Deep Teal text and buttons on Sky.

Do: one category, one colour.

Every dark band on a category page takes that category's colour. The header and the home page stay in the master palette; the home gateway shows each category card in its own colour.

Don't: mix category colours.

No second category colour on a page, no Yellow section ground (the Longevity Figma hero is Yellow: it becomes Forest). Product colours mark their product with a dot or an edge; they never carry text or data and never replace the category colour.

The closing CTA band takes the category colour; the footer is the same on every page, Mist with the Dark subscribe button (R-48, R-114); two dark bands never touch (R-119). Current

Page spec.

Fill this before designing or building a new page. The developer handoff lists the pages in scope; each one starts here.

Page:            (name and URL)
Status:          Launch / Phase 2 / Planned
Goal:            (one action the page asks for)
Audience:        (who arrives here and from where)
Template:        Category / Product / Inner / Landing
Sections:        (in order, from the templates above)
Copy status:     Draft / Legal review / Approved
Required lines:  "Assessment only. Not a diagnosis." · provider named · "[charge line · operations]"
                 under the hero button · the provider-approval line under treatments · safety info (product pages)
Rx names:        Where they appear (navigation, product page only)
Images:          (slots, see below; placeholders marked)
Motion:          (cards from the Motion page)
Figma nodes:     (desktop, mobile)
Mobile (390):    What differs from desktop: layout and order, type sizes, line breaks,
                 what stacks or hides, tap targets (44 minimum), safe areas (R-107)
Approvers:       Brand (Avi) always; Clinical with medical content; Legal for claims,
                 offers, consent and required lines (How we work · Who approves what)
Open items:      (each with an owner)

Image slots.

Until a licensed photo exists, every image frame is a labelled slot: "IMAGE · what it shows". Same radius as the final photo (16), same crop, Mist fill.

A slot never ships. It tells the developer and the photographer exactly what goes there, and keeps the layout honest while photos are pending (R-39).
